The Covariate Bradley-Terry Model (CBTM) extends classical Bradley-Terry by incorporating per-comparison covariates Zijk, allowing for contextual modeling such as home advantage. The model defines the probability of team i beating team j as a logistic function of their latent merit difference βi − βj plus a linear combination of covariates weighted by γ. This formulation supports both static and dynamic inference depending on how Zijk varies. The MLE is derived through score equations involving expectations μijk(β, γ), which are solved iteratively using an alternating algorithm. The existence of solutions depends on the configuration of covariates in the convex hull of the data. Bias correction improves finite-sample performance, especially for γ estimates. Asymptotic normality allows for statistical inference. The alternating Newton-Kantorovich method provides a robust computational approach, leveraging the structure of the problem to ensure convergence. These primitives enable GSE to compute accurate win probabilities while accounting for situational factors, and GSI to perform Bayesian inference on these parameters with calibrated uncertainty.
